summary: C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

Caixi Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti studied at Presidency University (~1928–1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, he held curatorial and superintendent posts at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India, and National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his BA and PhD at Harvard and studying at EPHE and DIAS. He was Victor S Thomas Professor at Harvard (1959–2003) and Distinguished Professor in Residence at UCLA (2003–2013).

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Indiana University Bloomington, Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford, Bailey completed an MA under Bryan J. Cuevas at Florida State University and a doctorate supervised by Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yudru Tsomu. Warner has held academic posts at Dickinson College, Middlebury College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz works in religious studies and Japanology. After earning an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, Foltz became a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University's Weatherhead East Asian Institute (attested 2026).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he has held posts at Cambridge, SOAS, Oxford, the Bodleian Library, and Hamburg.
Carel Gabriel Cobet studied at the Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1830–1836). A scholar of linguistics, he held appointments at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.
Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965). He held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, earning a PhD from UC Berkeley (~1972–1980). A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he served on the editorial board and as emeritus professor at Stanford University.

Carl Cappeller studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, and at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD), and Jena (Habilitation). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he became a professor at the University of Jena in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from ~1814 to 1816 and subsequently held a post there from ~1820 to 1864.
Carl Darling Buck was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, the University of Göttingen under Lichtenberg and Heyne, and the University of Helmstedt (PhD). From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor at Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.
Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung studied medicine at the University of Basel (1895–1900). Working in religious studies and medicine, he held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1913), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Olson is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who was mentored by John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer. Active in religious studies and linguistics, he served as Lektor (1847) and professor (1857) at the University of Oslo.
